The petitioners have filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against respondents seeking compensation on account of death of one (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.8/2025 Sri.Ravikumara.K.S S/o Sanghappa, who died in Motor Vehicle Accident.
02.

The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
On 13.12.2024 at about 12.30 p.m, when said Ravikumara.K.S was proceeding in his Honda Activa Scooter bearing No.KA-43-Y-4362 slowly and cautiously on the road from Bengaluru towards Devanahalli, when he reached near Kannamangala Gate, at that time a XUV 700 Car bearing No. KA-50-MC-7749, driven by its driver, at high speed, in rash and negligent manner and dashed against scooter of said Ravikumara.K.S from behind.

Due to impact, he fell down and sustained grievous injuries and immediately after the accident he was shifted to Akash hospital,
Devanahalli, but he succumbed to the injuries enroute to the hospital.
At the time of accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 53 years and was agriculturist by profession and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners are put to great financial loss and mental agony.
The petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioners No.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased.
The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending car and in this (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.8/2025 regard the Devanahalli Traffic Police have registered a case against driver of car.

The respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of offending car, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with costs and interest at the rate of 12% p.a.
03.
On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels, but only the respondent No.1 has filed objections.

04. The respondent No.1 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioners and further denied alleged accident, negligence of the driver of offending car, involvement of car in the alleged Girija vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 3 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4678040/
2 accident, age, avocation, income of the deceased, nature of the injuries sustained by the deceased and expenses incurred by the petitioners and further denied issuance of policy in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of Car bearing No.KA-50-MC-7749 and its validity since it is not been confirmed by the concerned policy issuing office.
If the owner of the vehicle were to produced the original policy before the court and their liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

The petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties and contended that the respondent No.2 had (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.8/2025 been willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence to drive the same as on the date of accident.

Similarly the respondent No.2 allowed to ply his vehicle on the road without having valid permit and fitness certificate and hence there is breach of terms and conditions of the policy and violation of M.V. Act and the compensation claimed is highly excessive, exorbitant and hence pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.1.
05.
On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, the following Issues has been framed:-
ISSUES 01.
Whether petitioners proves that they are the LRs/dependents of deceased Sri.Ravikumar K.S S/o Sangappa?

02. Whether petitioners proves that deceased Sri.Ravikumar K.S S/o Sangappa was died on13.12.2024 at about 12.30 p.m, on Kannamangalapalya Gate, B.B. Road,
Devanahalli Taluk, Bengaluru Rural District, due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing registration No.KA-50-MC-7749 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
03.
Whether respondent No.1 proves that driver of car not having valid license?
04. Whether respondent No.1 proves that due to the negligence of the deceased accident took place?
Whether respondent No.1 proves that the owner and Insurance Company are necessary parties?
06. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
07. What order or award?
06. The petitioners in order to prove their case, petitioner No.1 is examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 15 documents as Ex.P.1 to 15 and closed their side evidence.

To prove the said facts, she has produced notarized copies of Driving licence, Aadhaar cards of deceased and other petitioners as per Ex.P.11 to 15, which shows that petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioners No.2 and 3 are the major daughter and major son of the deceased.
As per the recent Judgment of our Hon'ble High Court even the major sons and married daughters are entitled to claim compensation for the death of their parents on all heads.
Hence, this tribunal is of the opinion that petitioners No.1 to 3 are the legal representatives and dependents on the income of the deceased.
Hence, I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.

The oral and documentary evidence adduced by the petitioners clearly goes to show that the accident has occurred due to the negligence on the part of the driver of offending car and deceased sustained injuries and later died enroute to the hospital.

Accordingly,
Issue No.2 is answered in the affirmative.
12. Issues No.3 to 5:-

In order to avoid repetition of facts and appreciation of evidence on record,
these issues are taken together for common consideration and discussion.
13.

The respondent No.1 has taken specific contention that the driver of the car was not having (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.8/2025 valid licence and accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased who rode his Motor Cycle in rash and negligent manner and petitioners have not made owner and Insurance Company of their Scooter as necessary parties.

But in this regard the respondent No.1 did not examine any witnesses nor produced any documents and also in Charge sheet the Investigation Officer has clearly stated that the offending vehicle came from behind and dashed to the Motor Cycle of the deceased which clearly goes to show that the negligence is on the part of driver of the car itself and further in Charge sheet has not quoted any sections regarding non-possessing of driving licence by the driver of the offending car.

When the accident was caused by the driver of offending car who came and dashed against the Motor Cycle from behind, the question of impleading owner and Insurance Company of the deceased Motor Cycle as parties does not arise at all.
Accordingly, Issues No.3 to 5 are answered in the negative.
14. Issue No.6:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Ravikumar.K.S, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
The PW.1/petitioner No.1 has stated that prior to accident deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 53 years and was agriculturist by profession and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners are put to great financial loss and mental agony.
15. It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The petitioners have not produced any birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card of the deceased to show exact date of birth of the deceased.
However, they have produced Ex.P.11 Driving licence and Ex.P.12 Aadhaar card of deceased.

Eventhough the said documents are not authenticated documents for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of other evidence,
said documents can be relied upon and according to which the date of birth of the deceased is mentioned as 01.01.1971.
The alleged accident occurred on 13.12.2024 and hence it appears that as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner is 54 years.

16. In order to prove the avocation and income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents.

Therefore, in the absence of satisfactory documents in proof of the income of the deceased, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2024 to be taken as Rs.16,500/- p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal assessed the monthly income of deceased is at Rs.16,500/-.

In the case on hand, undoubtedly the petitioner No.1 is the wife and petitioners No.2 and 3 are the children of the deceased and they are the dependents on the earnings of the deceased.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay Sethi & Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.

Therefore, considering the materials available on record, this tribunal is of the opinion that since there are two dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/3rd of the income towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (Rs.18,150 - Rs.6,050) = Rs.12,100/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.12,100/-.
As the deceased was aged about 54 years, the multiplier of 11 would have to be applied.
Consequently the claimants would be entitled for a sum of (Rs.12,100 x 12 x 11) Rs.15,97,200/- is awarded towards loss of dependency.
